clue.text: See 5
Swans around in glamorous Bochum

indicators.note: turning around means the letters are taken in the opposite direction, upwards here
the answer sits inside the run of words that follows, spanning the gap between them

parts.note: the end of glamorous and the start of Bochum

explanation.surface: Elegant swans gliding about in the German city of Bochum.
explanation.definitionFit: A cob is the male of the swan, so cobs are swans of one sex.

clue.text: Speaker's platform for Hague or Cameron, say

indicators.note: what a speaker says is heard rather than seen, so the word wanted only matches by its sound

parts.note: a pier is a landing platform jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A podium for one of two Conservative politicians to address the Commons from.
explanation.walkthrough: William Hague and David Cameron, former Tory leaders, both now sit in the House of Lords; 'Speaker' also hints at the Commons Speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Both men were made members of the House of Lords, so each is an example of a member of the peerage.

clue.text: Excessive sandwiches left, as well as filling of pate in roll

indicators.note: to sandwich something is to hold it between two outer layers, so this word goes round what follows

parts.note: undue means more than is warranted
standard abbreviation

indicators.note: the filling of something is its centre, so only the middle letters of the next word are used

parts.note: the two central letters of pate

explanation.surface: A complaint about an overstuffed bread roll, with pâté and more crammed inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roll' looks like the bread from the surface, but it is the verb: to move in waves. 'as well as' simply adds the second insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: To undulate is to move with a wave-like rising and falling motion, as the sea rolls.

clue.text: See 24
Environmental process which makes additive addictive?

parts.note: surface reading: something that turns a food additive into a habit-forming one
setter's reading: put the letter C, the chemical symbol of the element, inside 'additive' and keep it there, and you get 'addictive'

explanation.surface: A wry question about what turns a harmless food additive into something addictive.
explanation.walkthrough: C is the symbol for carbon; seizing a C and holding it inside 'additive' spells 'addictive', which is literally what the green technology's name describes.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the technology that traps emissions from power stations and locks them away underground to fight climate change.

clue.text: One needing oxygen stood up, admitted to A&E

indicators.note: a patient admitted to a hospital goes inside it, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: the letters of the hospital department name

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the word from bottom to top

parts.note: bore as in tolerated, past tense of bear

explanation.surface: A breathless patient who has been stood up and admitted to casualty.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E, accident and emergency, is the British hospital casualty department. 'stood' means endured, not got to one's feet.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerobe is an organism that requires air to live, the opposite of an anaerobe.

clue.text: When one has a mop, with tidying up required?

definitions.text: When one has a mop, with tidying up required?

parts.words: When one has a mop, with tidying up required?
parts.note: surface reading: a cleaning day, mop and bucket in hand
setter's reading: a mop is a shock of unruly hair, and the tidying needed is to that tangle on one's head

explanation.surface: Sounds like a housework day, out with the mop to clean up.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a day when one's hair will not behave, and by extension any day when everything goes wrong.

clue.text: Where to see Kim Kardashian's silhouette and rear? Hoot wildly

indicators.note: acting wildly is acting without order, so the letters are thrown into a new sequence
a silhouette is only an outline, so just the outside letters of the name are kept

parts.note: first and last letters, ignoring the possessive
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about where to view Kim Kardashian's famous curves and backside.
explanation.walkthrough: The Kim is not the reality star but Kim Jong Un, the dictator.
explanation.definitionFit: The country is ruled by Kim Jong Un, so it is the place where that Kim is to be found.

clue.text: Measurements of pants, say, worn by Democrat

indicators.note: clothing worn by someone goes around them, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: pants as a verb, gasps; 'say' flags it as an example
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Taking the size of the trousers a Democrat politician is wearing.
explanation.walkthrough: Pants here are not trousers but gasps for air.
explanation.definitionFit: Breadths are widths, measurements taken from side to side.

clue.text: Capitalist concerned with career regressing

indicators.note: to regress is to go backwards, so the combined letters are read right to left

parts.note: re means about or regarding
to career is to rush headlong, to dart

explanation.surface: A capitalist whose job prospects are going backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'career' looks like a noun for one's job but is the verb meaning to hurtle.
explanation.definitionFit: A dealer who buys and sells for profit is a capitalist in the everyday sense of a businessperson.

clue.text: Chatter about drug smuggled into American customs

indicators.note: contraband smuggled into a place ends up inside it, so these letters go within the next piece

parts.note: standard abbreviation

indicators.note: turning about means facing the other way, so the word is written backwards

parts.note: to gas is to talk idly
E for ecstasy

explanation.surface: Gossip about narcotics slipped past US customs officers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'customs' reads as the border service, but it means habits.
explanation.definitionFit: Usages are established practices or conventions, just as customs are.

clue.text: Metal band supports a barrel and tub containing litres

indicators.note: a thing containing something holds it inside, so one letter goes within the first piece

parts.note: to back is to support
standard abbreviation
taken as written
B is a dictionary abbreviation for barrel
a bathtub

explanation.surface: A metal hoop holding together a barrel and a tub of liquid.
explanation.walkthrough: A metal band sounds like a hoop on a cask, but it is a heavy metal group, the Birmingham band fronted by Ozzy Osbourne.
explanation.definitionFit: The group are pioneers of heavy metal music, so they are a band in that genre.

clue.text: Like a prophet doomed to stifle right expression of despair

indicators.note: to stifle something is to smother it, enclosing it completely

parts.note: fated means destined, doomed
standard abbreviation
a sigh expresses dejection

explanation.surface: A doomed prophet, like Cassandra, smothering cries of despair.
explanation.definitionFit: A prophet foresees the future, and being far-sighted means having vision about what lies ahead.

clue.text: Spin around a thousand times, inspiring German car racer

indicators.note: inspiring literally means breathing in, so the outer pieces take another inside

parts.note: to eddy is to swirl round
K for kilo, a thousand
the multiplication sign
short for Mercedes

explanation.surface: Spinning round a race track a thousand times in a German car.
explanation.walkthrough: The car is a red herring for the racer: the answer is the Belgian cyclist, and the Merc is breathed in between the swirl and the thousand times.
explanation.definitionFit: Eddy Merckx, five-time Tour de France winner, is widely seen as the greatest cycle racer ever.

clue.text: See 5
Marry a second time, and that's no joke

definitions.meaning: second meaning: an exclamation meaning honestly, seriously

explanation.surface: Getting married again is no laughing matter.
explanation.definitionFit: To ally is to join in union, so re-ally is to wed again; the adverb also insists something is said in earnest.

clue.text: Bits of information on King Ferdinand who was England's defender

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece placed on another comes after it

parts.note: R for rex, king
computer bits are ones and noughts, which look like the letters I and O

explanation.surface: Snippets of data about King Ferdinand, cast as a historical defender of England.
explanation.walkthrough: King Ferdinand suggests a Spanish monarch, but Ferdinand is a footballer's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Rio Ferdinand was a centre-back for Manchester United and the England national football team.

clue.text: Take drugs with my boss, looking rather shabby

parts.note: to do drugs is to take them
gear is slang for drugs
the setter's boss is the crossword editor, ED

explanation.surface: A confession of a drug binge with the boss, leaving both looking worse for wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my boss' is the setter speaking: a compiler answers to an editor.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog-eared book has corners folded down from wear, so it looks worn and shabby.

clue.text: Modest Mussorgsky's finale preceded by silence

indicators.note: being preceded by something means coming after it, which fixes the order of the two pieces

parts.note: the call for quiet

indicators.note: a finale is the closing part, so only the end letter of the name is used

parts.note: the last letter of the composer's name

explanation.surface: The end of a piece by the Russian composer Modest Mussorgsky, followed by a hush.
explanation.walkthrough: Modest is the composer's first name in the surface, and the adjective in the cryptic reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A shy person is reserved and self-effacing, which is what modest means.

clue.text: Fiery compiler running into Volkswagen Beetle's back

indicators.note: something running into a vehicle ends up within it here, so these pieces go inside the car

parts.note: the Passat is a VW model
the setter refers to themself as I
a machine that is running is on

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter

parts.note: end letter of Beetle

explanation.surface: A hot-tempered crossword setter crashing into the rear of a VW Beetle.
explanation.walkthrough: The Beetle is another VW, but only supplies its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A passionate person has strong, intense feelings, as a fiery temperament does.

clue.text: Only half decent police siren may do so

indicators.note: keeping only half a word means losing its other half, here the front three letters

parts.note: taken as written before cutting
ICE is the US Immigration and Customs Enforcement agency

explanation.surface: Only some officers are decent; a police siren may signal as much.
explanation.walkthrough: The siren is not on a police car but the mythical singer who lured sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sirens of Greek myth lured sailors with song, which is to tempt or lure, as the verb means.

clue.text: Welcomed by people in party, record cover song

indicators.note: a guest welcomed by hosts is taken in among them, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: members of the Green Party
the card sleeve an LP comes in

explanation.surface: Partygoers welcome someone, and an album cover's song is played.
explanation.definitionFit: Greensleeves is a traditional English folk tune, popularly but doubtfully credited to Henry VIII.

clue.text: The King has energy to replace current and present workforce

indicators.note: one thing coming in to replace another means swapping a single letter out for a new one

parts.note: Elvis Presley, the King of rock and roll
standard abbreviation in physics
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Elvis wielding fresh energy to take over the current workforce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' is not 'current' but a gift: Santa's workshop staff.
explanation.definitionFit: In Christmas lore Santa's helpers are the little folk who make the toys, the gift-making labour force.

clue.text: Attitude to Labour, with changeable Keir hot and cold

parts.note: W is a common abbreviation for with

indicators.note: something changeable can be altered, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
C for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A dig at Labour leader Keir Starmer blowing hot and cold on his party's stance.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour with a capital L suggests the political party led by Keir Starmer, but it means toil.
explanation.definitionFit: A work ethic is a person's belief in the value of diligent effort, their stance towards toil.

clue.text: Scheduled arrival times for letters from overseas

definitions.meaning: first meaning: estimated times of arrival, as abbreviated
second meaning: plural of the seventh Greek letter

explanation.surface: The expected landing times of mail flown in from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: ETA stands for estimated time of arrival; eta is also a character of the Greek alphabet, foreign script.

clue.text: Poisonous substance picked up, creating alarm

indicators.note: something picked up by the ear is heard, so the answer only matches by its sound

parts.note: a toxin is a poison

explanation.surface: A poison detected by monitors, setting off an alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: A tocsin is an alarm bell or warning signal, an old word for a sounding of danger.

clue.text: Get utterly wasted, say, in party I held in public

indicators.note: something held in another is enclosed by it

parts.note: overt means open, done in public
taken as written
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Admitting to getting completely drunk at a party held in public view.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdo it is to go too far, and drinking oneself senseless is one example of such excess.

clue.text: Prevent drinking that's wrong, but far from sinister?

indicators.note: something drinking takes a thing inside itself

parts.note: to deter is to prevent or discourage
a cross marks an error

explanation.surface: Stopping wrongful drinking, by someone who is anything but menacing.
explanation.walkthrough: Sinister is the Latin and heraldic word for left, so far from sinister points to the opposite side.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry dexter means the right-hand side, the counterpart to sinister, the left.

clue.text: Kudos when cracking the Guardian's puzzles

indicators.note: cracking something breaks it open, so the letters are broken up and reformed

parts.note: taken as written
the newspaper speaking of itself as we, so ours is US

explanation.surface: Praise for solvers who crack the newspaper's puzzles.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudokus are Japanese number-placement grids, a kind of logic puzzle printed in the paper.
